terra.problem: It says Bartimaeus used his voice because he could not see and calls it the one thing he had. The text gives neither claim.
It guesses why Bartimaeus did not send a message. Reasons for his actions cannot be added, even as a guess.
It says Bartimaeus was not hoping the crowd would slow down, but the text does not say what he hoped about the crowd.
It says Bartimaeus did not wait for anything. The text says he cried out louder, but does not make that broader claim.
It says Bartimaeus’s voice got Jesus to stop, assigning a reason for Jesus stopping that the text does not state.
It adds a specific time interval and treats the people calling Bartimaeus as the same people who told him to be silent. The text establishes neither.
It says staying put was the crowd’s old plan, but the text says people told Bartimaeus to be silent, not to stay where he was.
It says Bartimaeus did not shuffle or take his time. The text says he jumped up and came to Jesus, but does not describe how he made his way to Him.
It says Bartimaeus had no second thoughts, which the text does not say.
The explanation of Rabboni uses a fact from outside the passage without a reference, such as John 20:16.
It says Bartimaeus came to Jesus just fine. The text does not describe whether he had any difficulty coming to Him.
It says Bartimaeus did not turn around, but the text does not describe which way he was facing or how he began following Jesus.
It says Bartimaeus’s family is not mentioned, but Mark 10:46 identifies him as the son of Timaeus.
